title: Flexion and Extension
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. The detector over collects on purpose: mark anything that is teaching rather than clinical direction as NOT_CLINICAL rather than deleting it.

positions.as_written: Record two numbers and name the deficit, because an arc alone conceals fixed flexion.
Expect effusion to limit flexion early, and reassess range once it has settled rather than recording a limited range as fixed.
Treat the flexion arc as the product of surface geometry and ligament length, and note that surgery can alter either independently.
Measure extension deliberately rather than as part of a sweep, since small deficits are both the hardest to measure and the most disabling.
Record passive and active range separately when assessing a stiff knee, because the difference localises the cause.
Consider slope and offset when a knee does not achieve its expected arc after surgery.
Avoid quoting a design's published flexion as a patient's expected flexion.
